date_note: The Guyana Times page gives only its publication day; the court dates of the new charges are not stated.
exec: Police in Guyana say CCTV footage was removed from a police surveillance system without authorisation; charges now include the opposition leader.
geo_basis: Georgetown, Guyana, where the police surveillance system and court are
plain: Guyana's opposition leader was charged with aiding misconduct in public office over police CCTV footage allegedly copied without authorisation. Two constables face related charges.
summary: Guyana Times reports that police allege CCTV footage of an October 12 shooting was removed from the Guyana Police Force's Safe Country surveillance system without authorisation. Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed is charged with aiding and abetting misconduct in public office, and Constables Ashton Chapelle and Ryan Greene face related charges. The report says all three already faced cybercrime charges, and Mohamed and Chapelle remain on remand.
title: Guyana: opposition leader Azruddin Mohamed faces new charge over police surveillance footage, Guyana Times reports

validation.note: Single publisher (Guyana Times); the allegations are the police's, reported from court proceedings.

review.note: Compared charges, names, Safe Country system, Oct 12 footage, remand wording with Guyana Times
